name: Bridges, Castles & Bazaars
edition: 3rd edition in our project's sense = WikiCarpedia 'C2': Hans im Glück 2017 (German 'Brücken, Burgen und Basare', (c) 2010, 2017), Z-Man English 2018 ((c) 2010, 2018), new tile art by Anne Pätzke. 12 land tiles = JCloisterZone tile set bridges-castles-and-bazaars:2 (the garden edition). components.name: Land tiles
components.notes: 11 layouts (BB/Cccc.b twice). 8 tiles show a bazaar (BB/Cccc.b x2, BB/CFc.b, BB/CFR.b, BB/F.b, BB/R.bi, BB/RFR.b, BB/RFR.bi). 2 tiles have an inn (BB/R.bi, BB/RFR.bi), 2 a monastery (BB/LCFc, BB/LRFr), 1 a garden (BB/CFR!G, 3rd edition only). No tile has a coat of arms (pennant). Each tile carries the expansion mark, a small dark bridge-arch icon (decoration only).

components.name: Castle token
components.notes: Cardboard. 3rd-edition look: a roundish blob of meadow about one tile across with a white-stone castle on it (keep and towers with blue slate roofs, a small red flag, a ring wall around a courtyard). It is laid over a completed two-tile city of two semicircular caps (centred on the shared edge) and the knight is stood on it. See the rules file for castle rules.

components.name: Wooden bridge
components.notes: Brown wooden arch (a beam on two legs with a round opening). Laid straight N-S or W-E across one tile; both feet must stand in a field at the edge midpoints. Acts as a road segment. See the rules file.

tiles.name: Full city with bazaar
tiles.art: The whole tile is city: packed red-roofed, half-timbered houses on sandy-brown lanes, no walls or gates on any edge (it continues the neighbouring cities on all four sides), a few small green trees between the roofs. The bazaar fills the middle: a cluster of market tents (a yellow awning and a red-and-white striped tent in front, green-and-white and blue tents and white canopies with bunting behind, crates, barrels and sacks) on a patch of trampled brown earth, box x 0.33-0.78, y 0.37-0.70, centre (0.55, 0.53). One of the two copies also has a round white stone tower with a conical blue-slate roof and a small blue-roofed annex just north of the bazaar (box x 0.53-0.68, y 0.08-0.36; WikiCarpedia calls it a 'water tower'); the other copy has houses there instead (no scan of it found). No coat of arms on either copy. 1st edition: same layout; the bazaar is a yellow oval with three blue and pink canopy stalls right of centre (x 0.47-0.83, y 0.35-0.62), houses in clusters around it, no tower.

tiles.name: Three city caps, road into the east cap

features.note: ends at a gatehouse in the east city cap

tiles.art: Three separate city caps, none with a coat of arms: a north cap (wall from the NW corner to the NE corner, lowest at y 0.20), a west cap (wall from the NW corner to the SW corner, bulging east to x 0.22) and an east cap (wall from the NE corner to the SE corner, bulging west to x 0.75); each has blue-roofed wall towers with red roofs behind. The caps meet only at the NW and NE corner points: they are three different cities. The road enters at the S edge (0.52, 1.0), runs north to about (0.48, 0.55), then hooks east and ends at a gatehouse in the east cap's wall at (0.75, 0.50) (a road ending at a city gate). A dark green shrub stands inside the hook, in the small south-east meadow (x 0.50-0.68, y 0.50-0.72). Meadows: the big one lies west of the road and reaches north between all three caps (touches the S edge west of the road, borders the W cap, the N cap and the part of the E cap above the gate); the small one is the pocket east of the road between the road, the east cap and the S edge (borders only the east cap). 1st edition: same topology; the N cap is a thin strip with a gatehouse and the road curves up to a gate higher on the E cap (about (0.73, 0.28)).

tiles.name: City band with bazaar
tiles.art: One city crossing the tile from W to E (both full sides): its north wall runs from the NW corner to the NE corner sagging to y 0.18, its south wall from the SW corner to the SE corner arching up to y 0.80; blue-roofed towers along both walls, red-roofed houses inside. Thin lens-shaped meadow caps along the N edge and the S edge. The bazaar (market tents on brown earth, as on BB/Cccc.b) stands inside the city in the middle: box x 0.28-0.72, y 0.35-0.70, centre (0.50, 0.53). It is decoration inside the city and splits nothing. No coat of arms. The expansion mark is printed in the north meadow. 1st edition: same layout, the yellow bazaar oval in the upper middle of the band (x 0.35-0.75, y 0.25-0.55), a round tower and gate towers on the south wall.

tiles.name: Pointed city with gate road and garden

features.note: pointed 'witch-hat' segment: not semicircular, so it can never be part of a small city turned into a castle (HiG 7/2010; JCZ castle-base=false)
ends at the city gate in the diagonal wall

tiles.art: The 'witch-hat' city (WikiCarpedia C2 tile I). The city covers the whole W edge and narrows to a point in the NE corner. Its north wall runs just below the N edge from the NW corner to the NE corner (dipping to y 0.13), leaving a thin meadow strip along the N edge. Its other wall is an almost straight diagonal from the SW corner to the NE corner with a gatehouse in the middle at (0.50, 0.52). Red and blue roofs inside, towers along the walls. The road comes in from the E edge (1.0, 0.53) and runs west to end at that gate (about (0.53, 0.52)). The diagonal wall above the road, the road and the E edge enclose a triangular meadow touching the E edge between the NE corner and the road. Everything south of the road and the diagonal wall is one big meadow, and in it lies the garden: a rectangular flower bed seen at an angle (rows of red, purple, yellow, blue and white flowers inside a low border), box x 0.40-0.88, y 0.68-0.92, centre (0.64, 0.80). No coat of arms. Because the city's tip touches the NE corner, the N strip and the small triangle are separate fields. Outline = Inns & Cathedrals 'C!' (layout.js capSpike) turned so that the city sits on the west: capSpike at rot 3 gives exactly a N strip about 0.14 deep and a diagonal from just below the NE corner to the SW corner. 1st edition (BB/CFR!, same features minus the garden): the diagonal wall bulges towards the south-east so the gate and the road end lie near the E edge (about (0.80, 0.48)), the N strip is deeper (about 0.2) and the expansion mark sits in the south meadow where the garden is now.

tiles.name: City cap with road to a bazaar
tiles.art: A city cap along the N edge (wall from the NW corner to the NE corner, lowest at y 0.21, blue-roofed towers, red roofs behind). The road starts at the S edge (0.49, 1.0) and runs straight north to end at the bazaar. The bazaar (market tents on brown earth) sits a little below the centre, box x 0.27-0.75, y 0.38-0.72, centre (0.51, 0.55); it does not touch the city wall (a band of meadow lies between them). So one meadow surrounds the bazaar and the road end and borders the city. No coat of arms. Expansion mark bottom right. 1st edition: the same, with the yellow bazaar oval at x 0.22-0.77, y 0.43-0.80.

tiles.name: Meadow with bazaar
tiles.art: Plain meadow, no road or city. The bazaar (market tents on brown earth) stands up and left of centre: box x 0.17-0.65, y 0.12-0.50, centre (0.40, 0.31). Lower right a farmhouse: a long thatched half-timbered house with a smaller shed beside it and a few bushes, set diagonally, box x 0.53-0.92, y 0.63-0.92 (decoration; WikiCarpedia's 'farmhouse' illustration). Expansion mark bottom centre-left. 1st edition: the bazaar sits in the centre (x 0.22-0.80, y 0.35-0.68) and there is no farmhouse.

tiles.name: Monastery in a city

features.note: stands inside the city; monk and knight are independent

tiles.art: City band from W to E as on BB/CFc.b: north wall from the NW corner to the NE corner sagging to y 0.17 with a thin meadow cap along the N edge; south wall from the SW corner to the SE corner rising to y 0.76, with two gate towers, and a meadow cap along the S edge. In the middle of the city stands a church/monastery (red tiled roof, a square stone tower with a red pyramid roof at its west end, doors facing south), box x 0.33-0.75, y 0.30-0.72, centre (0.53, 0.50), its foot against the south wall. Red-roofed houses and blue-roofed towers fill the rest of the city. The monastery is a separate feature inside the city: the city still runs unbroken from W to E around it (one city, not two), and the church touches no tile edge. Keep the knight spot in the city away from the church (e.g. west part, about (0.15, 0.45)) and the monk spot on the church. No coat of arms. Expansion mark in the south meadow. 1st edition: same layout, church a little lower (x 0.28-0.72, y 0.30-0.80).

tiles.name: Monastery with curving road
tiles.art: A church/monastery (red roof, square tower with a red pyramid roof at its west end, entrance facing south-west) stands just above the centre, box x 0.20-0.77, y 0.20-0.72, centre (0.48, 0.46). The road enters at the W edge (0, 0.52), swings down in a wide U below the church to y 0.87 at x 0.48 and climbs back to the E edge (1, 0.50); it touches neither the church nor the S edge. It is one road from W to E (not two roads ending at the monastery). The church stands in the north meadow (W-north, N, E-north); the south meadow is the crescent below the road. Bushes at the church's foot. Expansion mark bottom left. 1st edition: same (church a bit higher, bottom of the U at y 0.88).

tiles.name: Road with inn ending at a bazaar
tiles.art: One meadow with a dead-end road. The road starts at the S edge (0.49, 1.0) and runs north-north-east to end at the bazaar in the upper right (market tents on brown earth, box x 0.36-0.85, y 0.12-0.50, centre (0.60, 0.31)); it meets the bazaar at about (0.58, 0.48). West of the road stands the inn: a red-roofed half-timbered house with a smoking chimney, box x 0.10-0.40, y 0.47-0.70, centre (0.25, 0.58), and below it its lake (blue pond), box x 0.18-0.42, y 0.75-0.93, centre (0.30, 0.84). The inn belongs to this road. Expansion mark bottom right. 1st edition: same layout (bazaar x 0.33-0.92, y 0.10-0.45; inn and lake in the lower left; a bush left of the bazaar).

tiles.name: Two roads ending at a bazaar
tiles.art: The bazaar (market tents on brown earth) sits in the upper left: box x 0.13-0.60, y 0.12-0.47, centre (0.37, 0.30). A short road comes in from the N edge (0.50, 0) and ends at the bazaar's north-east side (about (0.45, 0.14)); a second road leaves the bazaar's south side (about (0.33, 0.47)), curves east to about (0.57, 0.62) and then runs south to the S edge (0.50, 1.0). The bazaar ends both roads: two separate roads, not one through road. The two roads and the bazaar split the meadow into a west part and an east part. In the east meadow: highwaymen, two robbers (red and purple-blue clothes) lurking behind a dark green bush, box x 0.70-0.90, y 0.65-0.85 (decoration only; WikiCarpedia's distribution list wrongly calls it a garden, see the notes). A small round shrub in the SW corner. Expansion mark bottom, left of centre. 1st edition: the bazaar lies in the lower middle (x 0.28-0.88, y 0.55-0.82), so the N road is long (with a bush beside it) and the S road is a short stub; no robbers.

tiles.name: Two roads to a bazaar, with inn

features.note: ends at the bazaar; only this road has the inn

tiles.art: The bazaar (market tents on brown earth) sits in the upper middle: box x 0.20-0.66, y 0.13-0.48, centre (0.43, 0.30). A short road from the N edge (0.53, 0) ends at its top (about (0.50, 0.14)); a second road leaves its bottom (about (0.45, 0.48)) and runs down with a slight S-bend to the S edge (0.53, 1.0). East of this south road stands the inn (red-roofed two-winged building), box x 0.62-0.90, y 0.47-0.67, centre (0.76, 0.57), with its lake below it, box x 0.68-0.94, y 0.73-0.95, centre (0.81, 0.84). The inn belongs only to the south road. A few white-flowered shrubs north-east of the bazaar (about (0.78, 0.36)). The roads and the bazaar split the meadow into a west part and an east part. Expansion mark bottom, left of centre. 1st edition: same layout (bazaar x 0.12-0.70, y 0.12-0.42; inn and lake in the lower right; a bush in the west meadow).

setup: Shuffle the 12 land tiles (8 show a bazaar) into the land tiles; with The River they go into the land stack, never the river stack. Land deck with all seven expansions: 71 + 18 + 24 + 30 + 18 + 12 = 173 tiles. [RB-DE3 p.1]

Each player gets a personal supply of bridges and castle tokens: 3 + 3 with 2-4 players, 2 + 2 with 5-6 players (6 players only with Inns & Cathedrals). Spare pieces go back in the box; a player with none left cannot build. [RB-DE3/EN3 p.1]

The three parts may be used separately (RB-DE3 p.1 'komplett oder teilweise'): app options bcb.bridges, bcb.castles, bcb.bazaars (default: all on) and bcb.auction (default on; off = the official no-bidding bazaar variant, RB-DE3 p.6). With bazaars off a bazaar is only a picture; with castles off small cities just score; with bridges off nobody has bridges.
Scores may become negative (bazaar bids). Results, ranking and the score track must allow it. [RB-DE3 p.5]
The inns printed on BB/R.bi and BB/RFR.bi (south road only) count only when Inns & Cathedrals is also on; otherwise they are decoration. [WikiCarpedia BCB tile notes; MASTER BC14]
turn_sequence: Step 0 (start of turn): also at the start of EVERY bazaar-round turn - the fairy gives that player +1 and the once-per-turn ransom allowance starts afresh (a bazaar-round turn is a full turn). Not for the host's builder part 2 after a bazaar round, which belongs to the host's original turn. [RB-DE3 p.5 'einen normalen Zug'; OC* C. Tisch BGG 570930; JCZ FairyPhase]

Step 1 (draw): in a bazaar-round turn you take your bought tile instead of drawing. A tile counts as placeable if it fits as printed or with one of YOUR bridges. If every legal placement needs a bridge you may throw the tile away and draw again (also a bought tile). A bought tile that fits nowhere is removed and you draw from the stack (normal draw rules); if nothing can be drawn your bazaar turn is skipped. [OC 10/2014; JCZ TilePhase]

Step 2 (place): the tile and at most one bridge are ONE choice. Then 2b builder trigger (evaluated after the bridge), 2c tower foundation, 2d volcano, 2e bazaar mark: a drawn (not bought) bazaar tile placed while no bazaar is running marks an auction for the end of this part. [RB-DE3 p.1, p.4; OC WiCa T&B (bridge triggers the builder)]
Step 3 (ransom, Tower): never during an auction; needs at least 3 points, so a negative score cannot pay. [Tower EN p.3; MASTER B17]

Step 4 (follower step): a figure may stand on a bridge built on the tile just placed (road rules); the portal may target an unoccupied, unfinished bridge road on another tile; the fairy may move next to one of your castellans; castellans can never be captured or removed by the princess. [RB-DE3 p.2, p.6; MASTER B4]
Step 5 (dragon flight): castellans, bridges and castle tokens are never eaten; a figure on a bridge stands on its tile and is eaten. [P&D EN p.3, p.6]

Step 6 (scoring): 6a castle decisions - for each small city completed by this placement whose single knight's owner still has a castle, that owner chooses castle or 4 points (seat order from the active player); 6b score the completed features as usual (converted cities are not completed; unoccupied completed features are recorded at full value); 6c every waiting castle built BEFORE this placement whose area holds part of a feature from 6b scores (best value; chains); 6d return figures, lonely builder/pig check. [RB-DE3 p.3-4; JCZ phase order Dragon -> Castle -> Scoring]

Step 6 1/2 (bazaar): if this part marked one and at least as many drawable tiles as players remain, reveal one tile per player, auction them, then the bazaar round: from the host's left to the host every player plays a full turn with their tile (builder part 2 drawn at once; a dragon tile flies at once; bazaars placed during the round are ignored). [RB-DE3 p.4-6; RB-EN3 p.5; OC 2/2021]

Step 7 (builder part 2): if the host's bazaar tile earned the double turn, part 2 is played after the whole bazaar round. A bazaar drawn in that part 2 is held after it. [RB-DE3 p.6; WiCa FAQ] (The reverse order - CAR 5/2013, JCZ, accepted by HiG 08/2016 as an alternative - is not adopted.)
Step 8 (end of turn): after a bazaar round the next normal turn is the host's left neighbour, so nobody gains or loses a normal turn. [RB-EN3 p.5]

Game end: the game never ends inside a bazaar round (a draw that fails there only skips a part 2 or a replacement); it ends when the host's part 2 or the next normal turn finds no tile. Before final scoring every castellan goes home with 0 points and no fairy +3. [RB-DE3 p.4; MASTER BC46]
placement: A bridge runs straight across ONE tile, north-south or east-west, from the middle of one edge to the middle of the opposite edge; never diagonal. [RB-EN3 p.1; JCZ Location.BRIDGES]

Both ends of a bridge must stand on printed FIELD edges of that tile (never a city, road or river edge). In between it may cross anything: a city, a road, a river, a monastery or garden, figures. [RB-DE3 p.1-2 figures; RB-EN1 p.3]

Where: on the tile just placed or on a tile sharing a side with it (not diagonal). At most one bridge per tile (so no crossing bridges) and at most one bridge per tile placement (two in a builder double turn, one per bazaar-round turn). You need a bridge in your supply. [RB-DE3 p.1; S-CAR fn 361; JCZ]
After the bridge is in, every edge between neighbouring tiles must match: each bridge end continues a road (or bridge) already on the board or faces an empty square. [OC 12/2014]

A tile may be placed so that a road runs into a field edge if the bridge built with it carries the road on: a bridge on the NEW tile when the new tile shows field where a neighbour's road arrives (one bridge can fix both of its ends), or a bridge on the NEIGHBOUR when the new tile's road runs into the neighbour's field edge (the neighbour's far end must then face an empty square). Only road-against-field mismatches can be fixed, and only one bridge per placement. [RB-DE3 p.1-2 figures 1-3; OC 12/2014]

Consequence (proved, and checked over 100,000 random placements): a spot and rotation that fit only with a bridge fit with exactly ONE bridge position, and a bridge that is not needed always has both ends facing empty squares - it starts a new road and never touches an existing road. [MASTER H.2.3]

An optional bridge is allowed even when the tile fits without it, on the new tile or on a neighbour (there it runs parallel to the shared side). [RB-DE3 p.1; OC* C. Tisch BGG 542577; S-CAR fn 356] JCZ offers optional bridges on the new tile only; not adopted.

A tile that fits ONLY with a bridge is placeable (it is drawn normally), but the player may throw it away and draw again instead. A tile with at least one bridge-free placement must be placed. Without a bridge left such a tile is simply unplaceable (removed, draw again). [OC 10/2014; JCZ TilePhase]

A bridge never splits a field or a city; it only adds a road (the last feature of that tile). The field under it keeps both halves of the bridged edge, so the two fields beside a road that ends at a bridged edge join through it. [RB-DE3 p.2]
Bridges stay for the rest of the game and belong to nobody once built. [RB-DE3 p.1; Tower EN p.4]

Rivers: a bridge end is never on a river edge, but a bridge may cross the river between two field edges (spring RI/s, the straights RI.1/IFI, the lake RI.1/I.e). Bridges are allowed during the river phase, including one that lets a river tile's road meet a field edge; all river rules still apply and the river still splits the fields. [RB-DE3 p.1; RB-EN1 p.3 caption; JCZ]

Small city (castle base): a completed city of exactly two tiles, each contributing one semicircular one-edge cap. Not eligible: the pointed city of BB/CFR!G, the wedge city of IC/C! and the princess city of DG/CCc+.p (city property castle_base: false -> engine noCastle). Every other one-edge cap qualifies, including the large 3rd-edition caps, BB/CCCR's three caps, TO/RCr and the River caps. No one-edge cap in our tile sets has a pennant or goods, so a small city is always worth 4. [RB-DE3 p.3; OC 7/2010 (C. Tisch, BGG 538079); WikiCarpedia; JCZ castle-base]

Castle area: the castle's 2 tiles plus the 2 squares beside each of them across the castle's long sides - a 2x3 block. Castle on (x,y)+(x,y+1): those two and (x-1,y), (x+1,y), (x-1,y+1), (x+1,y+1); castle on (x,y)+(x+1,y): those two and (x,y-1), (x,y+1), (x+1,y-1), (x+1,y+1). Empty squares belong to it; tiles placed there later count. [RB-DE3 p.3 figure; JCZ Castle.getVicinity]
A castle separates fields exactly as the small city did. [RB-DE3 p.4]
followers: A meeple, large meeple or builder may stand on a bridge only if the bridge is on the tile just placed; it is the normal single figure of the turn and follows road rules (the whole road must be unoccupied; the builder needs your meeple or large meeple in that road). Never the abbot or the pig. A bridge on a neighbouring tile takes no figure that turn. [RB-DE3 p.2, p.6; WiCa examples 6-7]
The bridge is built before the follower step, so a bridge that joins your new road to an occupied road stops you from claiming that road this turn. [RB-DE3 step order; JCZ]

Castle decision: the owner of the small city - the player whose single knight (meeple or large meeple) is in it, possibly not the active player - chooses to score 4 or to build one of their castles on it. The knight moves onto the castle and becomes its castellan. It does not matter whether the knight stood on the first cap or was placed on the second one this turn. [RB-DE3 p.3, p.6]

No castle left: no choice, the small city scores 4. No knight in it: no castle, it is just completed. In our expansions a small city never holds more than one follower; the engine offers a castle only when exactly one follower is present. [RB-DE3 p.3; JCZ CastlePhase]
No figure is ever placed on a castle (it is not a feature of a new tile) or on a bazaar. [RB-EN3 p.4]

The castellan goes home when its castle scores. If the castle never scores, it is removed before final scoring. Castellans are never eaten, captured, removed by the princess or targeted by the portal. [RB-DE3 p.3-4, p.6; P&D EN p.6; Tower EN p.4]
scoring_during_game: A bridge scores like a road segment on its tile: 1 point per tile (2 if the road is an inn road). A tile counts once even if the road crosses it twice (printed road and bridge). [RB-DE3 p.2 (6-point example); WiCa 2/2014]
An inn affects only the printed road beside it; a bridge's road is an inn road only when it is connected to a printed inn segment. [OC FAQ 1/2021]

Small city: its owner chooses between scoring 4 and building a castle. A converted city is NOT completed: no points, no fairy +3, no goods, and it does not count as a completed city for other castles. [RB-DE3 p.3]

A waiting castle scores at the first placement, after the one that built it, that completes a road or city with any tile in its area, a monastery or garden whose own tile is in its area, or another castle (chain). Builder part 2 and bazaar-round turns count as later placements. Fields never trigger; an abbot recall never triggers; final scoring never triggers. Scoring is mandatory. [RB-DE3 p.3-4; WiCa fn 13 ('a later round of scoring') and trigger table (gardens); JCZ]
Who completed the feature and whether anybody scores it does not matter: unoccupied roads, cities, monasteries and gardens trigger at their full value. [RB-DE3 p.4; WiCa 2/2015]

Value: the full points of the feature as scored, pennants and bonuses included - road 1/tile (inn 2), city 2/(tile+pennant) (cathedral 3), monastery or garden 9, a small city that was scored 4. Never the fairy's +3, never goods. The feature's owner and the castle owner both score; owning both pays twice. A large-meeple castellan scores once. [RB-DE3 p.3-4, p.6; WiCa 4/2014]

Several features finish in a castle's area at once: the castle owner takes one; the engine takes the highest (no other effect). One feature may trigger several castles; each scores the full value. [RB-DE3 p.4; WiCa fn 18; JCZ]

Chains: a castle that scores counts as a completed feature for every other waiting castle whose area contains one of its two tiles (direction matters); those score the same value; repeat until nothing new scores. A castle reachable from several values takes the highest. Every castle scores at most once. [RB-DE3 p.4; WiCa fn 20; JCZ scoreCastles]
After scoring, the castellan goes home and the castle stays on the board, complete; it never scores again. Breakdown bucket: castle. [RB-DE3 p.3]

Bazaar auction: reveal one tile per player. The player left of the host chooses a tile and opens with a bid of 0 or more. Each other player without a tile, clockwise from the chooser, may raise (strictly higher) or pass, once. Then the chooser buys (pays the high bidder and takes the tile) or sells (the high bidder pays the chooser and takes it). If nobody raised, the chooser pays his bid to the bank. Breakdown bucket: bazaar. [RB-DE3 p.5]
Bids are whole points and may be higher than your score; scores may go below 0 (app limit: 99 per bid). [RB-DE3 p.5]

Whoever has a tile is out of this bazaar. The next chooser is the next player clockwise after the previous chooser who has no tile yet (after a sale the turn to choose moves on). The last player without a tile takes the last tile free. [RB-DE3 p.5; WiCa fn 26; JCZ] RB-EN3 'from the previous buyer' is not adopted.
scoring_end: First, every castellan still on a castle goes home: 0 points, no fairy +3. End-of-game scoring never triggers castles. [RB-DE3 p.4; WiCa (fairy)]

Fields: every castle bordering a field (scored or not) is worth 4 to that field's winner instead of 3, and 5 to a winning farmer owner with a pig there. A castle counts once per field. [RB-DE3 p.4, p.6; S-CAR fn 375; JCZ Field.getCityPoints]
Incomplete roads with bridges score as usual: 1 per tile, 0 if it is an inn road (I&C). [RB-DE3 p.2; MASTER A.4]
edge_cases: The tile fits only with a bridge and the player does not want to use one: throw it away and draw again. [OC 10/2014]
A bridge end facing an existing tile is legal only if that tile shows a road there, which is possible only for a bridge on the new tile. [OC 12/2014]
A second mismatch elsewhere (another side, a city or river edge) can never be fixed: one bridge per placement. [RB-DE3 p.1]
A road over a bridge and along the printed road of the same tile: the tile counts once. [WiCa 2/2014]
No second (crossing) bridge on a tile. [RB-DE3 p.1]
No figure on a bridge built on a neighbouring tile. [RB-DE3 p.2; WiCa ex. 7]
A bridge on a neighbouring tile can never finish a road (its far end always faces an empty square). [derived; MASTER H.2.3]
Bridges may be built on a volcano tile or on the dragon's tile; no figure may then stand on that bridge. [WiCa P&D; MASTER B3/B15]
Small city with a pointed, wedge or band-like cap (BB/CFR!G, IC/C!, DG/CCc+.p): no castle; it scores 4. [OC 7/2010; JCZ]
Small city completed by an opponent: the knight's owner decides. Owner without castles: it scores 4. [RB-DE3 p.3]
One tile completes two small cities: each owner decides separately, in seat order from the active player. [derived; JCZ]
The princess, a tower capture or the dragon removed the small city's knight before step 6: no castle. [MASTER step order; JCZ]
Unoccupied small city completed in an older castle's area: it is a completed city worth 4 and triggers that castle. A small city converted there does not. [RB-DE3 p.3-4]
A feature completed by the placement that built the castle does not trigger it. [RB-DE3 p.3; S-CAR fn 368]
Castle built in builder part 1, feature completed in part 2 (or in a bazaar-round turn): it triggers. [WiCa fn 13; JCZ]
Unoccupied monastery or garden completed in the area: triggers at 9. A monastery whose neighbours lie in the area but whose own tile does not: no trigger. [RB-DE3 p.4]
Inn road or cathedral city triggers: the castle gets the doubled/tripled value. [RB-DE3 p.6]
Waiting castle at game end: castellan removed, 0 points; the castle still gives farmers 4 (5 with a pig). [RB-DE3 p.4, p.6]
Bazaar tile discarded (unplaceable, or thrown away because it fitted only with a bridge): no auction. [OC 10/2014]

Fewer drawable tiles than players: no auction (with P&D before the first volcano, dragon tiles in the stack do not count). Exactly as many: the auction uses them all and the game ends after the bazaar round. [RB-EN3 p.5; JCZ]
A dragon tile revealed while the dragon is not in play is set aside and replaced. [P&D EN p.2; MASTER B22]

A bazaar placed during a bazaar round (bought, a replacement draw, or a builder part 2 inside the round) is ignored; the host's own part 2 after the round is outside it. [RB-DE3 p.5; OC 2/2021; WiCa FAQ]

Builder triggered by the host's bazaar tile: auction and whole bazaar round first, then the host's part 2. Builder triggered by a bought tile: part 2 drawn from the stack at once, before the next bazaar-round player; empty stack -> no part 2, the round goes on. [RB-DE3 p.6; OC* BGG 498317]

Dragon tile placed in the bazaar round: the dragon flies at once (movers from that player), then the round continues. A volcano placed there brings the dragon and returns the set-aside tiles to the stack. [RB-DE3 p.6; MASTER B22]
Bought tile unplaceable: removed, the player draws from the stack, no refund; nothing to draw -> that bazaar turn is skipped (no fairy +1). [JCZ; derived]
Bid above your score: allowed, scores go negative. Only the chooser bid: he pays the bank. [RB-DE3 p.5]
Ransom with a score below 3 (also negative): not allowed. No ransom or any other action during the auction. [Tower EN p.3; MASTER B17]

base: Bridges may cross printed roads at right angles (straight road tiles, monastery with road) without meeting them; fields stay as printed apart from the joins at bridge ends. [RB-DE3 p.2 figure 4]
All base one-edge caps (E, H, I, D, J, K, L and their garden versions) can form small cities. [RB-DE3 p.3]
Base gardens (3rd edition) may be bridged; with The Abbot gardens trigger castles like monasteries. [RB-DE3 p.2 figure; WiCa trigger table]
river: Bridge ends never on river edges; a bridge may cross the river between two field edges (RI/s, RI.1/IFI, RI.1/I.e); bridges are allowed during the river phase, also to let a river tile's road meet a field edge. The river still splits fields. [RB-DE3 p.1; RB-EN1 p.3; JCZ]
River caps (RI.1/CICI, RI.1/CIRI) can be halves of a small city. A bazaar can never happen during the river phase (bazaar tiles are land tiles, drawn only after the river).
abbot: The abbot never stands on a bridge or a castle. [base supplement; RB-DE3 p.6 lists]
Gardens trigger castles exactly like monasteries: the garden's own tile must be in the area, empty gardens count (9). [WiCa trigger table; JCZ Garden implements Monastic]
An abbot recall never triggers a castle (the feature is not completed; MASTER B1); its later completion does. [MASTER B1; JCZ]
Bridges over gardens and monasteries are allowed; an abbot or monk underneath stays. BB/CFR!G carries a garden. [RB-DE3 p.2 figure 4]
inns-cathedrals: The large meeple may stand on a bridge and may be a castellan (one castellan: the castle pays its value once; fairy +1/+3 flat). [RB-DE3 p.6; I&C official 'it may be big, but it's still only one person']
Inn and cathedral bonuses count for castle scoring (castles never score at the end, so the 0-point rule never applies to them). [RB-DE3 p.6]
An inn affects a bridge only through connection to its printed road; BCB's own inns count only with I&C on. [OC 1/2021; WiCa tile notes]
6 players (I&C): 2 bridges + 2 castles each; 6 tiles revealed at a bazaar.
traders-builders: The builder may stand on a bridge of the tile just placed (with your meeple in that road); never in a castle; no builder can ever be in a small city. [RB-DE3 p.6; derived]
A bridge that brings the new tile into your builder's road triggers the double turn. [OC WiCa T&B; S-CAR fn 57]
Pig: a castle is worth 5 to a winning farmer owner with a pig in that field. [RB-DE3 p.6]

Bazaar and builder: the host's part 2 comes after the bazaar round; bought tiles may trigger their owner's builder (part 2 drawn at once); bazaars drawn inside the round are ignored. Goods: moot (no cap has goods; a converted city would give none). [RB-DE3 p.6; OC 2/2021; OC* BGG 498317]
Fairy +1 and ransom: once per turn; each bazaar-round turn is a turn of its own; the host's part 2 shares the host's original turn.
princess-dragon: The dragon never eats castellans, bridges or castle tokens; it may enter castle tiles and eats figures on bridges. [P&D EN p.3, p.6; RB-DE3 p.6]
The princess cannot remove a castellan (a castle is not a city). A princess removal of the small city's knight comes before the castle decision. [S-CAR fn 94; MASTER order]
A dragon tile that completes a small city: the flight comes before the castle decision; if the knight is eaten there is no castle. [MASTER order; JCZ]
The portal may put a meeple on an unoccupied, unfinished bridge road on another tile; never onto a castle; never the dragon's tile. [JCZ; MASTER B4]

Fairy: may stand by a castellan (+1 per turn, +3 when the castle scores during play, nothing at the end); a fairy assigned to the knight that becomes castellan stays assigned; her tile (which the dragon may not enter) is the tile the knight stood on. [RB-DE3 p.6; WiCa; JCZ]

Bazaar: revealed dragon tiles are set aside while the dragon is not in play; a dragon tile placed in the bazaar round flies at once; a volcano placed there reinserts the set-aside tiles (seeded RNG). Fairy +1 at the start of every bazaar-round turn. [P&D EN p.2; RB-DE3 p.6; MASTER B22]
Bridges may be built on a volcano tile or the dragon's tile (no figure on them). A small city completed by a volcano tile may become a castle (the castellan is not on a tile). [WiCa P&D; derived]
tower: A tower can capture a figure on a bridge, never a castellan; bridges and castles are neutral and never captured. [Tower EN p.4; RB-DE3 p.6]
A bridge and a tower may share a tile; a castle may cover a cap with a foundation; the tower keeps working. [RB-DE3 p.6; WiCa]
Ransom: never during an auction; allowed in your own bazaar-round turn; needs at least 3 points (negative scores cannot pay). [Tower EN p.3; MASTER B17]
Tower actions are allowed in bazaar-round turns (full turns). [OC* BGG 570930]

edition_differences: 1st edition (HiG 2010 'Burgen, Brücken und Basare') vs 3rd edition (HiG 2017 'Brücken, Burgen und Basare'): same components, counts and rules. The 3rd edition orders everything by turn step (bridge with the tile, castle in scoring, bazaar after the turn), says 'only 1 bridge per tile', removes castle meeples explicitly before final scoring, allows bids above your score, and adds a page on other expansions. Tiles: new art; BB/CFR! became BB/CFR!G (garden).
Z-Man English 2013 (1st-edition text) errors: 'Bazaar (12 tiles)'; 'a player may not bid more points than he has'; 'two city end segments'.

Z-Man/HiG English 2018 departs from the German original: small city 'only 2 tiles'; no 'in a later turn'; no knight moving onto the castle; 'you decide what order they are scored'; 'next player clockwise from the previous buyer'; 'starting with the first buyer'; builder 'completes' instead of 'extends'. It adds the too-few-tiles rule (adopted).
Fairy in a castle: allowed by Big Box 3 (1st edition), forbidden by a late 1st-edition clarification, allowed again by the 3rd-edition rulebook (adopted).

Builder and bazaar: CAR 5/2013 (a mistranslation) and JCZ play the builder's part 2 before the auction; HiG called that a valid alternative in 08/2016; the 3rd-edition rulebook says bazaar round first (adopted).
'Castles & Bridges' (HiG 2025, C3.1) is a different expansion (16 tiles, neutral bridges worth 3, no bazaars) and is not implemented.
ai_hints: Bridges are scarce (2-3 per game): use one when a tile only fits with it and the move is worth more than the bridge (cost about 1.2-2.5 points, higher with the last bridge, lower late in the game). If a bridge-only tile is worth nothing to you, throw it away instead.

Mandatory bridges that join two roads or carry your road over a city are the valuable ones; a bridge also joins the two fields beside a road that ends at the bridged edge - count it for farm majorities. Optional bridges that only start a new road are rarely worth a bridge.

Castle or 4 points: build the castle when the most likely FIRST completion in its 6 squares is clearly worth more than 4 (a monastery or garden with 6-7 neighbours, a big city or road about to close, another waiting castle), at least ~15 tiles remain and you have meeples to spare. Score the 4 if a cheap road or small city could be closed there next turn, or late in the game.

Against opponents' castles: close a cheap feature in their area to cash them in low; do not complete a big feature there unless you gain more than they do. A big completion in your own castle's area pays twice.
Bazaar: value each revealed tile for each player (best immediate placement and follower value) once per auction and cache it - the board does not change during the auction.

Chooser: pick the tile best for you relative to what you would get otherwise; open with 0. When a rival raised to b: buy if (your value - fallback) + (rival value - rival fallback) > 4b, otherwise sell (relative score swing).

Bidder: raise by one only while (your value - fallback) >= the new bid (you may be sold the tile at that price); being paid for a raise the chooser buys over is profit. With 2 players every point moves directly between you.
The last tile is free: in 3+ player games waiting can pay. A tile that would complete an opponent's big feature is worth denying.
No-bidding variant: take the tile with the highest value for you.
rules.kid_rules_text: BRIDGES, CASTLES & BAZAARS. BRIDGES: You have 3 bridges (2 with 5 or 6 players). When you place a tile you may build ONE bridge, on your new tile or on a tile right next to it. It goes straight across, side to opposite side, and both ends must stand on grass - never on a city, road or river. In between it can cross anything. A bridge is a road worth 1 point per tile, and it never cuts a field or a city in two. A bridge can rescue a tile: your tile's road may run into grass if your bridge carries it on. A tile that only fits with a bridge may also be thrown away. Your meeple may stand on a bridge on your new tile. CASTLES: When a tile finishes a tiny city of two half-round pieces, the player whose knight is in it chooses: 4 points, or build a castle there. The knight climbs onto the castle, which watches 6 squares: its two tiles and the two beside each. On a LATER tile, the first road, city, monastery or garden finished there (a monastery or garden must sit on one of the squares) gives the castle's owner the same points - even if nobody owned it! Then the knight comes home. If several finish at once, the castle takes the best, and a scoring castle can set off its neighbour. Castles still waiting at the end score nothing, but every castle is worth 4 to farmers. BAZAARS: After a turn with a bazaar, turn over one tile per player. Starting on the left, a player picks a tile and bids (0 is fine). Everyone else without a tile may raise once. Then the picker buys it (paying the top bidder) or sells it (the top bidder pays the picker). Scores can even drop below zero! The last tile is free. Then everyone plays their tile as a normal turn, starting on the bazaar player's left.
figures: Bridge on the new tile: a road arrives at the field edge of a new city-band tile; an east-west bridge over the city carries it on (renderMini: [-1,0,'U',1,meeple], [0,0,'F',1, bridge 1], [1,0,'U',1]).

Bridge on the neighbouring tile: the new straight-road tile (with a meeple) meets the field edge of a city-band tile already there; the bridge goes on that tile and its far end faces an empty square ([0,0,'F',1, bridge 1], new [-1,0,'U',1,meeple]).
Not allowed: a north-south bridge on a straight road tile would stand on the road ends (red cross); second panel: a bridge end facing an existing meadow edge (red cross).
Bridges in a row: one over a monastery with a monk, one over a garden, carrying one road (RB-DE3 p.2 figure 4).
Road scoring: a 6-tile road with 2 bridges between two crossroads = 6 points, each tile once.
Fields join under a bridge: the meadows north and south of a road that ends at a bridged edge flow into the meadow under the bridge (one highlight colour).
Building a castle: two facing half-round caps, the second just placed, a red meeple; the castle covers both and the meeple stands on top. Inset: the pointed city of BB/CFR!G, crossed out.

Castle area: a 2x3 grid numbered 1-6 with the castle across 2/5 and square 4 empty; ticks on the monastery and road on 1, the city at the top of 3, the city on the right of 6; a cross on a monastery just outside whose neighbours are inside.
Castle scoring: Blue closes a 16-point city with one tile on square 6; the castle owner also scores 16 and the castellan comes home.
Castle chain: two waiting castles whose areas overlap; one completion scores both with the same points.

Bazaar: the revealed tiles in a row, the chooser's pick with an opening bid, one lap of raises, 'buy or sell?', the last tile free, then arrows for the playing order starting left of the bazaar player (the 3-player rulebook example).
End of game: a castellan lifted off ('0'); a farm next to a castle and a city: 4 + 3.

implementation_notes: Engine, AI, UI and tests: MASTER.md H.2-H.5. Expansion id 'bridges' (options.expansions.bridges); sub-options options.bcb = { bridges, castles, bazaars, auction } (absent = true).
Converter: castle_base: false on a city -> noCastle: true. Needed on BB/CFR!G feature 0 (here), IC/C! feature 0 (inns-cathedrals.json) and DG/CCc+.p feature 0 (princess-dragon.json).
layout_hint and refs on each tile are extra fields for layout.js and traceability; the converter ignores them. water_tower (one copy of BB/Cccc.b only) is decoration.
